Quercetin is linked to the Response regulator RamR, which is targeted by N-(1-benzyl-3,3,3-trifluoro-2,2-dihydroxypropyl)-acetamide, a compound that also targets the cGMP-gated cation channel alpha-1. Similarly, quercetin is associated with Small conductance calcium-activated potassium channel protein 3, which is targeted by the same compound and also leads to the cGMP-gated cation channel alpha-1. These findings indicate that quercetin may modulate the activity of the cGMP-gated cation channel alpha-1 through the activation of downstream signaling pathways involving RamR and other regulatory proteins. The consistent scores across the three paths suggest a robust relationship, but the exact mechanism of interaction remains to be fully elucidated. The evidence supports a potential role for quercetin in influencing the function of the cGMP-gated cation channel alpha-1, though further experimental validation is needed to confirm the direct interaction.
